question: What is the primary function of skeletal muscle?

options.A: Moving food along the digestive tract
options.B: Regulating the diameter of blood vessels
options.C: Generating voluntary movement of the body

explanation: Skeletal muscles attach to bones and contract consciously to move the skeletal system. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h1)

question: How do skeletal muscles contribute to body temperature regulation?

options.A: By circulating warm blood to the skin
options.B: By producing heat through metabolic activity
options.C: By evaporating sweat from the muscle surface
options.D: By insulating internal organs with fat layers

explanation: Muscle contraction requires energy, releasing heat that maintains core body temperature. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h1)

question: What connective tissue layer surrounds an entire skeletal muscle?
explanation: The epimysium is the outer fibrous layer wrapping the whole skeletal muscle organ. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h2)

question: A bundle of skeletal muscle fibers surrounded by perimysium is called what?
explanation: The perimysium groups individual muscle cells into distinct compartments known as fascicles. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is the specialized plasma membrane of a skeletal muscle fiber called?
explanation: The sarcolemma acts as the cell membrane for the individual muscle fiber. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the sarcoplasmic reticulum in muscle fibers?

options.C: Transmitting action potentials into the cell

explanation: The sarcoplasmic reticulum holds calcium until an electrical signal triggers its release into the sarcoplasm. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h3)

question: What protein makes up the primary component of thick filaments in a sarcomere?
explanation: Thick filaments are built from bundled myosin molecules with projecting heads. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h4)

question: What happens to the length of thin and thick filaments during muscle contraction?

options.A: They lengthen to span the expanding sarcomere space
options.B: They shorten significantly as the muscle contracts
options.C: They dissolve completely and reform after relaxation
options.D: They slide past each other and remain the same length

explanation: Contraction shortens the sarcomere because filaments overlap more, not because the filaments themselves change length. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which neurotransmitter is released at the neuromuscular junction to stimulate muscle contraction?
explanation: Acetylcholine is the specific chemical messenger that crosses the neuromuscular synapse to stimulate skeletal muscle fibers. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h5)

question: What role does calcium play once it is released into the sarcoplasm during muscle excitation?

options.A: It depolarizes the sarcolemma to start the action potential
options.B: It binds to troponin to expose actin binding sites
options.C: It physically links the thick and thin filaments together
options.D: It breaks down ATP to supply immediate mechanical energy

explanation: Calcium binding to troponin alters regulatory protein positions, clearing the path for myosin heads to attach to actin. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which energy pathway produces lactic acid as a byproduct during intense exercise without oxygen?
explanation: When oxygen supply is insufficient, glucose breakdown yields ATP and lactic acid anaerobically. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why is aerobic respiration the preferred pathway for long-duration endurance activities?

options.A: It generates instantaneous energy faster than creatine phosphate
options.B: It yields a high amount of ATP efficiently using oxygen
options.C: It prevents any accumulation of cellular waste products
options.D: It bypasses the need for glucose and glycogen stores

explanation: Aerobic metabolism in mitochondria extracts maximal ATP from nutrient molecules, sustaining prolonged activity. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which skeletal muscle fiber type is specialized for endurance and resistant to fatigue?
explanation: Slow oxidative fibers rely on aerobic respiration, featuring high myoglobin and capillary supply to resist fatigue. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h7)

question: A weightlifter performing short, maximal lifts relies primarily on which muscle fiber type?
explanation: Fast glycolytic fibers generate high power rapidly, making them ideal for short, intense bursts of strength. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h7)
